dedupe_keys.name: usgs economic effects model for the 2025 us list of critical minerals ofr 2025 1047

description: The model USGS used to rank mineral commodities by the economic harm of supply disruptions. Open-File Report 2025-1047 (August 2025, version 2.0 April 2026) says supply risk was judged on two criteria: the effect of trade disruption scenarios on the US economy and reliance on a single domestic producer. Post-disruption quantities and prices come from supply and demand elasticities and spare capacity for yearlong foreign trade disruptions, and a nonlinear optimisation with input-output tables estimates effects on US GDP for over 1,200 scenarios across 84 commodities, weighted by probability. The 215-page report is a free download with a Python implementation in an appendix and a data release. Coverage is the United States economy and world producers. Caveats: results depend on elasticity and probability assumptions. For simulation it links mineral supply shocks to industry output losses, reusable for other disruption scenarios. A related catalogue record is the USGS earthquake risk to copper and rhenium supply case study.
